winner.title: Yemen: how I made saltah

evidence.authenticity: Full dish with hilbeh (fenugreek) and zhug added at the end, eggs, potatoes, tomatoes. Uses minced beef and beef stock, a home-cook adaptation. Author is not Yemeni and gives little on the dish's roots.
evidence.precision: Most ingredient amounts are missing (meat, stock, fenugreek, cumin and cardamom have none). No pan sizes. Doneness cues are weak: browned meat, tomatoes softened 'a bit', simmer 40 to 60 minutes.
evidence.testing: The author cooked it and reports what went wrong: the pot was too small, the coriander went in too early, and the condiments belong at the end. No test kitchen.
evidence.photos: 9 captioned process photos covering hilbeh, zhug, frying onion and beef, tomatoes and potato, stock, and the finished dish.
evidence.efficiency: Condiments are made the night before and chilled, which uses parallel work well. Meat and onion are fried in a separate pan.
evidence.access: Fenugreek seeds are in US groceries and spice shops. No substitutions are given, but nothing is unobtainable.

winner.why: It has the only real process photos and a cook's own troubleshooting notes. Marty Made It is more precise on amounts but has no step photos.

runnerUp.title: 195 Yemen - Saltah

evidence.authenticity: Lamb, pressure-cooked or Dutch oven, served in a stone pot (haradha) or cast iron, with frothy hulba made by the author's mother's method (overnight fenugreek soak). Rice is added, which is a variant. No author bio.
evidence.precision: Most amounts are given, but the hulba list and its method disagree and the rice amount is missing. Cues: onion translucent, meat breaks easily, thick-soup consistency, bubbly. No pan size.
evidence.testing: Explains the fenugreek soak (removes bitterness) and gives pressure cooker and Dutch oven times. No test process.
evidence.efficiency: Pressure cooker cuts the cook to about 40 minutes.
evidence.access: Fenugreek has no substitute noted. Hulba and the stone pot are the only unusual items.

runnerUp.why: It is more precise on amounts but has no process photos and inconsistent hulba quantities.

notes: No test-kitchen or authority recipe exists. Most search hits are pages.dev scraper clones or a wasmer.app Cookpad mirror. The Remitly blog page has no structured recipe, and WebFetch dropped its connection, so it was not scored. The Spicery link returned 404. Food.com is a minced-beef version, and the best one read gives no pan sizes or many amounts. A better source may be a Yemeni cookbook or a Yemeni food blog not surfaced by search, such as yemeniyah.com, which had a fahsa recipe that is a different dish. Suggested retry: look for a Yemeni cook with amounts and process photos, or the Arousing Appetites page if it becomes reachable.
